items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: There was a Chinese boy who lives in New York now that I went to school with, Tommy Ewing.

ctx.x: The neighborhood that you lived in originally in Savannah, was that unusual in the South to have an integrated neighborhood at that time?

No, because actually at that time, except for maybe the Italians. But Indians, and Negroes, and even Chinese, they usually went to the same schools. There was a Chinese boy who lives in New York now that I went to school with, Tommy Ewing. And he has a sister, Olivia Ewing, and we all went to the same school, East Broad School in Savannah.

I never forgot that, you know.
But the Italians, they lived in that district, but they usually were on a section all by themselves over there. Uh-huh. But some strange things happened in the South in those days because I grew up with some Italian kids, and we got to be real good friends. And they were the Rekuparos. And, in fact, their father had a grocery store. And they couldn't -- they could just barely speak English, the father and the mother.
